bottom_line: In older patients with systolic ischemic heart failure, rosuvastatin vs placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.02).
implications: These data support that, over a median follow-up of 32.8 months, rosuvastatin lowered LDL cholesterol and hsCRP but did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in the primary composite endpoint (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.02; P = 0.12) or all-cause death (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.86 to 1.05; P = 0.31), while being associated with fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations (2193 vs 2564; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Randomized, placebo-controlled comparison of rosuvastatin 10 mg daily vs placebo in older patients with symptomatic ischemic systolic heart failure.
major_points.quote: A total of 5011 patients at least 60 years of age with New York Heart Association class II, III, or IV ischemic, systolic heart failure were randomly assigned to receive 10 mg of rosuvastatin or placebo per day.

major_points.text: Primary composite endpoint was cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke (time to first event).
major_points.quote: The primary composite outcome was death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.

major_points.text: No statistically significant reduction in the primary composite outcome with rosuvastatin.
major_points.quote: the primary outcome occurred in 692 patients in the rosuvastatin group and 732 in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83 to 1.02; P = 0.12)

major_points.text: No statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality.
major_points.quote: and 728 patients and 759 patients, respectively, died (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.86 to 1.05; P = 0.31).

major_points.text: Prespecified analysis showed fewer total cardiovascular hospitalizations with rosuvastatin.
major_points.quote: there were fewer hospitalizations for cardiovascular causes in the rosuvastatin group (2193) than in the placebo group (2564) (P<0.001).

major_points.text: Rosuvastatin lowered LDL cholesterol and hsCRP compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: patients in the rosuvastatin group had decreased levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (difference between groups, 45.0%; P<0.001) and of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (difference between groups, 37.1%; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Safety: no excess muscle-related or other adverse events were observed with rosuvastatin.
major_points.quote: No excessive episodes of muscle-related or other adverse events occurred in the rosuvastatin group.

criticisms.text: Authors state they did not investigate nonischemic heart failure or heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

criticisms.text: Authors note uncertainty about why rosuvastatin did not reduce the primary composite outcome.
criticisms.quote: We do not know exactly why rosuvastatin did not reduce the frequency of the primary compos­ite outcome.
